metaDescription: Six 5000 watt inverter generators compared by running output from 3900 to 4600 watts, tank size, noise, outlets and fuel type, for RV and backup buyers.
expertTake: The maXpeedingrods 5KW dual fuel holds the highest running figure in the group at 4600 watts on gasoline, while the AMERISUN 5000 is the pick for overnight runs thanks to a 3.43 gallon tank and a CO sensor. Anyone planning to run two air conditioners should skip this size and step up to a 6500 class unit or pair smaller ones.
introParagraphs: At five thousand watts a generator stops being a camping accessory and becomes a power plant you plan around. The case is bigger, the tank is bigger and the engine is a serious single cylinder that you need to treat with the respect it deserves. It is also the point where outlet limits start to cap what the machine can usefully deliver.

The headline number is again a peak, so the useful figures are the continuous rating, the tank behind it and whether the panel can spread that output across enough circuits. Those three decide whether the machine carries a whole camper or only part of one.

products.name: maXpeedingrods 5KW dual fuel inverter generator, 4600W rated
products.description:
The 4600 rated watts on gasoline are the highest continuous figure in this lineup, which means the 5000 label here is about as honest as it gets in the class. Propane drops the output to a 4000 watt class figure, a 600 watt loss that is bigger than the usual 10 percent, so plan loads around the lower number if you will run on LPG. The listing makes the economic case for propane: it is easier to get and to keep, and the cost per kilowatt hour is lower than gasoline.

The inverter section produces pure sine wave power, which protects electronics. With 4600 watts you can start a rooftop air conditioner while the microwave and lights run, and still have margin for a battery charger. Against the AMERISUN at 4000 running you gain 600 watts, and that is a different tier of capability, not a rounding error.

High output means high engine load, so oil changes should be on time and the air filter should be clean. Dual fuel adds a regulator and hose to the maintenance list. Because output on propane falls to 4000, keep gasoline on hand for the heaviest days. In a quiet park its high output also means the engine sits well above idle once a big load arrives, so expect more noise than the part load figures on smaller machines.
products.bestFor: Buyers who need the most continuous watts and want propane as a backup fuel.
pros: 4600 rated watts on gasoline, highest here
Propane option stores fuel for years
cons: Propane output drops to a 4000 watt class figure
Larger engine load demands on time oil changes

products.name: AMERISUN 5000W start, 4000W running inverter generator
products.description:
A 3.43 gallon tank with a listed 10 hours at half load is the headline, since half load here means 2000 watts for ten hours. That is the longest runtime in the group by a wide margin, and it comes with a carbon monoxide shutoff and a noise figure under 59 dBA. A 223cc overhead valve engine drives it, producing 5000 starting and 4000 running watts.

Total harmonic distortion is under 3 percent, so sensitive electronics are safe. The runtime claim is the one that matters for a furnace night or an outage, because you refuel once a day, not three times. It holds 600 fewer running watts than the maXpeedingrods, which is a sensible trade for longer unattended running.

A big tank means a big volume of gasoline that can go stale, so use stabilizer and plan on emptying it before a long storage period. The sub 59 dBA label is a part load claim, and a 223cc engine at full output is louder. Keep the CO sensor port clear of dust, and position the machine well away from the living space. Compared with the Oxseryn at 2 gallons, the extra tank means one fewer refuel through a night, which is the real everyday difference between the two.
products.bestFor: Overnight and outage users who value tank size and a CO shutoff.
pros: 10 hours at half load on a 3.43 gallon tank
cons: 600 watts below the top running figure
Large tank of gasoline to keep fresh

products.name: Westinghouse iGen5000 5000W peak, 3900W rated inverter generator
products.description:
The Westinghouse gives you the best interface in the group: a rotating LED panel that reports fuel level, power output, remaining run time and voltage, with a remote electric start and an auto choke that removes the guesswork on cold mornings. It rates 3900 watts and 5000 peak at under 3 percent distortion. The telescoping handle and wheels make the weight manageable on flat ground.

The 3900 rated watts are 100 below the AMERISUN, which is close enough that the display and remote start are the reasons to choose it. The panel has a TT-30R, a 5-20R duplex and two USB outlets. There is no 240 volt outlet, so the 5000 label cannot be delivered through a single plug.

The auto choke is a feature that avoids flooded starts, and it removes the most common cold weather failure. Remote start still depends on the starter battery, so keep it charged by running the engine monthly. Westinghouse parts and support are broadly available, which helps in year three. Since the 5000 label cannot come out of one outlet, split heavy loads across the TT-30R and the 20 amp duplex.
products.bestFor: Owners who want a readable display and easy starting at 3900 running watts.
pros: Rotating display shows load and runtime
cons: 3900 rated watts, below the top three

products.name: Westinghouse iGen5000DFc dual fuel inverter generator

specList.label: Fuel claim
specList.value: Up to 50% savings vs fixed speed

products.description:
This is the dual fuel version of the same Westinghouse platform, aimed at an RV, a jobsite or emergency home backup. The listing leans on a claim of up to 50 percent fuel savings from inverter technology that adjusts engine speed to demand, which is a comparison against a fixed speed generator and not against other inverters. The outlets are the same TT-30R, 5-20R and two USB ports.

The listing excerpt gives only the 5000 peak figure, so ask for the rated gasoline and propane numbers before comparing it to the maXpeedingrods at 4600 and 4000. What you buy is the Westinghouse interface plus the choice of fuel. A 20 pound cylinder in a shed stores indefinitely, and that is what makes it a backup machine.

Propane lowers output, so size the loads for the propane number. The regulator and hose are items to check each season, and gasoline should be rotated if you keep it in the tank. Compared with the single fuel iGen5000, you pay for flexibility you may never use, so decide honestly whether you will store propane.
products.bestFor: Backup owners who store propane and want the Westinghouse interface.
pros: Idle down inverter saves fuel at light load
TT-30R plus household outlet and USB
cons: Rated watts not stated in the excerpt

products.name: Mutaomay 5000W peak, 4000W running inverter generator
products.description:
A total harmonic distortion figure under 2 percent is the lowest in the group, and it matters if the generator will power a CPAP machine, a modern refrigerator board or a laptop. The output is 4000 running and 5000 peak watts, the same as the AMERISUN, so it competes with that machine on price and cleanliness. Noise is listed under 64.5 dB at 23 feet, louder than the 59 dBA claims above.

The tradeoff is that it lacks the long tank and CO shutoff that lift the AMERISUN. If your priority is power quality for electronics, it is the better choice, but if you sleep near the generator, take the CO protected unit. It is sold for home backup and RV use, so confirm the outlet types on the panel before you order.

Check the manual for the shutdown features before relying on them, since the listing excerpt does not describe them. Standard care applies: oil before each start, stabilized gasoline and a clean air filter. At 5 decibels louder than the AMERISUN, give it extra distance from the tent.
products.bestFor: Owners who care most about low distortion for sensitive electronics.
pros: Suitable for home backup and RV
cons: 64.5 dB is louder than the AMERISUN

products.name: Oxseryn 5000W peak, 4000W rated inverter generator, 60 lb
products.description:
This is the cheapest way into 4000 running watts, and the listing shows where the corners were cut: 70 dB noise, a 2 gallon tank and a 6 hour runtime at half load. Output is 4000 rated and 5000 peak, the same electrical numbers as the AMERISUN and Mutaomay. At 60 pounds it is light enough to carry, and Eco mode adjusts engine speed with the load.

The 70 dB rating is a clear statement that it is not a quiet machine, and the 6 hour runtime is 4 hours shorter than the AMERISUN's. For a work site or a backup unit that sits far from living space, those are acceptable compromises. For a campground with quiet hours, they are not.

Its value is raw watts for the lowest outlay. Plan a refuel at the 6 hour mark of any half load night, and keep an eye on the oil because the engine is loaded harder than a bigger tank machine would be. Use it where the noise rating is not a problem. Treat it as a tool for work and backup where cost matters most.
products.bestFor: Budget buyers who need 4000 running watts and can tolerate noise.
pros: 4000 rated watts at the lowest tier
cons: 70 dB is loud for a campground

buyingCriteria.explanation: At the 5000 label the continuous figures range from 3900 on the Westinghouse iGen5000 to 4000 on the AMERISUN, Mutaomay and Oxseryn, and up to 4600 on the maXpeedingrods. A 700 watt spread is bigger than a microwave. If you run an air conditioner with a heater or a microwave, favor the high end.

A 30 amp, 120 volt outlet delivers at most about 3600 watts, and a 20 amp outlet about 2400. A 4000 watt generator spreads its output across several outlets or needs a 240 volt plug to deliver everything. Check the panel for how you will connect your loads. Many buyers discover this only after a breaker trips on an overloaded duplex.

The AMERISUN's 3.43 gallon tank gives 10 hours at half load, while the Oxseryn's 2 gallons give 6. A half load figure is 2000 watts here, which is a typical overnight draw. Compare hours at the same load before you decide.

Propane reduces output, and the maXpeedingrods drops from 4600 to a 4000 class figure. That is 13 percent, more than the typical 10. Buy dual fuel if the machine rarely runs and you want fuel that stores.
Ratings range from under 59 dBA on the AMERISUN to 70 dB on the Oxseryn. That is a big gap and you can hear it. A bigger engine at full load is louder than the label.
THD under 3 percent is the standard, and the Mutaomay claims under 2. The Oxseryn open frame lists under 5 percent in a sibling listing. If you power CPAP or sensitive boards, prefer the cleanest.

howWeEvaluated.title: Continuous watts
howWeEvaluated.description: We ranked on rated figures: 4600 on the maXpeedingrods, 4000 on three units and 3900 on the Westinghouse. The gap decided the top places. Units that left the running figure out lost points.

howWeEvaluated.title: Runtime and tank
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared tank sizes and runtime claims at their stated loads. The AMERISUN's 3.43 gallons stood out. Different load bases were not compared directly.

howWeEvaluated.title: Controls and display
howWeEvaluated.description: We counted remote start, auto choke and displays as comfort features. The Westinghouse units lead. We checked that each had a recoil backup.

howWeEvaluated.title: Noise and safety
howWeEvaluated.description: We compared dBA claims and CO protection. The AMERISUN lists both a sub 59 dBA rating and a CO shutoff. The Oxseryn's 70 dB placed it last.

howWeEvaluated.title: Value and support
howWeEvaluated.description: We weighed watts per outlay and parts access. Westinghouse has the broadest support. Figures come from manufacturers' listings, not our measurements.

rows: Dual fuel with display and remote

cards.label: Single fuel
cards.text: The AMERISUN, Mutaomay, Oxseryn and Westinghouse iGen5000 hold full output on gasoline. Fuel must be rotated every few months.

cards.label: Dual fuel
cards.text: The maXpeedingrods 5KW and Westinghouse iGen5000DFc accept propane. The maXpeedingrods drops to a 4000 class figure on LPG.

howToChoose.note: Choose single fuel for regular use and dual fuel for backup.

cards.label: Look for
cards.text: A TT-30R outlet, enough running watts for one or two loads and a quiet rating. Remember a 30 amp plug limits one outlet to about 3600 watts.

cards.label: In this comparison
cards.text: The Westinghouse iGen5000 has the TT-30R and easy starting. The AMERISUN adds the long tank and CO shutoff.

cards.label: Spend more if
cards.text: You need the highest watts or a display. The maXpeedingrods 5KW and Westinghouse units provide them.

cards.label: Save if
cards.text: You need 4000 watts for a work site. The Oxseryn does it.

maintenance.why: A 223cc engine under load heats the oil. Fresh oil protects the bearings.
Bigger engines breathe more dust. A clogged filter fouls the plug.
Westinghouse remote start needs a charged battery. Run the engine under load for 20 minutes.
The maXpeedingrods and Westinghouse DFc use hoses. Soapy water shows leaks.
A 3.43 gallon tank of old fuel gums a carburetor. Stabilize or drain.

faq.a: No. It is a peak figure. Running watts range from 3900 to 4600 here.

faq.q: Can it run two air conditioners?
faq.a: A 4600 watt unit can in some cases, but two 13,500 BTU air conditioners start near 6000 watts together. A soft start kit lowers the surge and helps. For two units a larger machine or a parallel pair is the safer plan, and you can stagger the starts by a minute.

Most RV class inverter generators offer 120 volt only. A 30 amp outlet gives about 3600 watts, so the rest has to leave through the other outlets. If you need 240 volts for a well pump or a subpanel, look at the larger 6500 class machines.
For backup, yes. The maXpeedingrods loses about 600 watts on LPG.
The AMERISUN claims under 59 dBA at part load, and the Oxseryn 70 dB. Loaded engines are louder.

Change the oil after the first 20 hours and then yearly or per the manual. Clean the air filter more often in dust, and replace the spark plug each season. Run the engine monthly under load so the carburetor and starter battery stay healthy.
